## 8. Conclusions (hand-written section; every number quoted appears in the tables above / evidence map in section 7)

Scope for every claim below: template contexts, one concept (base verb ->
3rd person singular), level 0.9, primary metric kl, gemma-3-1b bf16 +
gpt2 fp32 + gemma-3-4b 4-bit, expanded symmetric templates (16+16
subjects), n_ctx=60, 3 seeds. Probe families are never pooled.

1. **Q2 - ESTABLISHED.** Park 2024's Cov^-1 pre-multiplication improves the
   raw unembedding-difference direction (`cau_unemb` < `euc_unemb` KL):
   positive in all 27 grid runs (9 per model) with CI lower bound > 0 in
   every one (gemma-1b +0.10..+0.11; gpt2 +0.74; gemma-4b +0.16), and
   unchanged under ridge_rel 1e-8/1e-4 (identical to 3 decimals), min_mass
   0.5, and the doubled step budget.

2. **Q1 - CONSISTENT DIRECTION, NOT ESTABLISHED.** The adaptive metric
   beats the Euclidean metric on the Dual MD probe (`dua_dmd` < `euc_dmd`)
   in 19/19 point estimates (9 gemma-1b, 9 gpt2, 1 gemma-4b) across seeds
   and alpha in {5e-3, 2e-2, 1e-1}; the CI excludes zero in 15/19 runs but
   crosses it for gpt2 at alpha=5e-3 and flips sign under the min_mass=0.5
   robustness setting (-0.16 [-0.333, -0.002]), so the task document's
   "established" bar (direction consistent across ALL specified robustness
   settings) is not met.

3. **Q4 - CONSISTENT DIRECTION, NOT ESTABLISHED.** Same pattern for
   `dua_dmd` < `cau_dmd`: 16/19 positive point estimates, CI excludes zero
   in 14/19 (all gemma-1b at 2e-2/1e-1, gemma-4b, 5/6 gpt2 at 2e-2/1e-1),
   exceptions: gpt2 at 5e-3 (-0.122, CI crosses 0) and min_mass 0.5
   (-0.144).

4. **Q3 - CANNOT ESTABLISH that the adaptive metric improves on the fixed
   metric on the unembedding-difference probe; the opposite direction holds
   at Park's alpha.** `cau_unemb` has lower KL than `dua_unemb` at
   alpha=5e-3 on all three models (gemma-1b -0.58..-0.63, gpt2 -1.34,
   gemma-4b -0.92; all CIs exclude 0 in this direction); at alpha >= 2e-2
   on gemma-1b the two are practically equivalent (differences +0.004..
   +0.030, inside the +-0.05 margin at alpha=1e-1), while on gpt2 the
   adaptive method remains worse (-0.38). In this setting a precomputed
   fixed metric on the unemb probe retains or beats the adaptive metric.

5. Metric divergence (reported, not averaged): the adaptive methods have
   the BEST rank-retention (`rd`) and pair mass (`cf`) in most runs even
   when their full-vocabulary `kl` is worse (see Tables 2/4); kl99 ~ kl
   (ratios 0.97-0.99, Table 5), so the long tail is not what penalizes
   them. Interpretations beyond this are exploratory.

6. Exploratory notes (hypothesis generation only): `cau_ctx` (fixed metric
   on the context probe) fails completely on gpt2 (reach 0.00 at every
   level including 0.5; near-singular S0 with ridge_rel 1e-6) while it
   works on gemma; `dua_ctx` needs alpha >= 5e-3 to reach (pilot). The
   min_mass=0.7 robustness cell could not be run: the target-side filter
   keeps 19/300 contexts (< 20), which the guardrail rejects by design -
   the current templates cannot support Park-style mass >= 0.7 filtering
   on the target side. Tightening to 0.5 removes the dual advantage on the
   dmd probe (see 2), suggesting the adaptive metric's benefit concentrates
   in less peaked starting distributions (exploratory).

7. Decision-tree outcome (task document section 6): Q1 holds in direction
   (with the min_mass caveat), so the follow-through was WP4 with focus on
   Q3/Q4. Summary: on the Dual MD probe the ordering adaptive > fixed >
   Euclidean is directionally consistent; on the unembedding-difference
   probe the fixed Park 2024 metric is the strongest single method in this
   setting, and the adaptive metric only matches it at alpha >= 2e-2 on
   gemma-1b.

## 9. Limitations (required by the task document)

- One concept (verb -> 3rd person), template contexts only; no natural
  text (C4) replication; conclusions must not be extrapolated.
- `rd` is a simplified variant of Park 2026's inverse-rank difference:
  top-0.99 set at the START only, not the union of top sets across steps.
- KL here uses a 1e-12 floor over (pair mass + neutral tokens); the
  authors add a 5e-3 offset - absolute KL values are not comparable to
  theirs (WP1, repro_check.md).
- Step size eta = 0.01*||lambda_0|| and stop at P1 >= 0.99 vs the authors'
  absolute step 2.0 (m) / 0.5 (e) and stop at 0.9999; per-step dynamics
  verified equivalent at matched step size (WP1).
- gemma-4b is 4-bit quantized (bf16 does not fit 8 GB) - self-consistent
  with saved lambda/G but not strictly the same model as Park's.
- alpha=5e-3 is taken from Park 2026 appendix B.2 without verifying the
  checkpoint/scale correspondence.
- Cluster bootstrap over 15-16 subject clusters: intervals remain coarse.
- Multiple comparisons: uncorrected (Q1-Q4 are pre-specified, everything
  else exploratory).
- WP1: the author's shipped m_steering lacks an F import and could not run
  as-is; numerical comparison used a one-line runtime injection of the
  obviously-intended import.
